title:
File tools that keep
you in control.
label: ABOUT FILECOMPRESSER
introduction: FileCompresser brings everyday compression, conversion and ZIP tasks into your browser. Choose a tool, review its settings, and save a copy you have checked. No tool account or file upload is required.
seoDescription: Meet FileCompresser: browser-based image, video, audio, PDF and ZIP tools, with local file processing, clear output sizes and practical limits.

sections.heading: Your device processes the file
body: The website downloads its interface and processing code. Your selected file is read and processed inside the browser tab, rather than sent to a compression server. Public tools do not require an account.

sections.heading: Actual bytes, clear outcomes
body: See input and output sizes together. Ordinary compression keeps an efficient original when no smaller result is found. A format conversion or new ZIP archive can be larger, and is labelled as a separate operation.

sections.heading: Review before replacing
body: Choose settings, cancel a run, compare supported image results and download the copies you need. Keep originals until you have opened and checked the output.

sections.label: THE TOOLKIT
sections.heading: Different files need different workflows.
body: The tools cover JPG/JPEG, PNG and still WebP images; GIF palette optimization; supported MP4/MOV compression; WebM-to-MP4 conversion; MP3 re-encoding; WAV-to-MP3 conversion; PDF structural optimization; and ZIP creation or extraction. A mixed-file tool selects the matching workflow for supported inputs.

The browser uses image workers and encoders, FFmpeg WebAssembly for media, pdf-lib for PDFs and fflate for ZIP tasks. Code is loaded when needed. PDF image downsampling and image resizing are not offered.

sections.label: PRACTICAL LIMITS
sections.heading: Useful results depend on the source.
body: Each tool lists its accepted formats and input limit. Queues allow up to 500 files and 300 MiB in total. Browser memory, image dimensions, codec support and file complexity can prevent processing even below those limits. Media jobs have a five-minute processing limit.

Lossy encoding changes image or sound information. No fixed reduction, processing time or quality score is promised. The aim is a valid output with honest feedback, rather than a smaller number at any cost.

sections.heading: Help us understand a problem
body: Use the contact page for troubleshooting and the configured support email. Include the tool, browser, approximate input size and exact error. Keep private file contents out of messages and screenshots; the public tools have no support-file submission form.

support.emphasis: Our guides explain formats, quality and file size.
